name: Dong Ding-Yu
forbes_bio: Dong Ding-Yu is the chairman and CEO of Elite Material, a maker of laminates and prepregs, key base materials for printed circuit boards.
It is the world's largest supplier of halogen-free laminates and prepregs by sales.
Dong worked as associate professor at San Jose State University before he was appointed director of Elite Material in 2001.
The company's Penang, Malaysia plant, its first production site in Southeast Asia, started operation in 2025.
forbes_facts: Dong's maternal granduncle, Ho Ying-Chin, was a top-ranking Nationalist China general and commanded the Chinese army during World War II.

name: Dylan Field
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2025)
forbes_bio: Dylan Field is cofounder and CEO of design software company Figma, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in July 2025.
Figma listed its shares at a fully diluted valuation (including outstanding equity awards) of nearly $20 billion. Its stock price more than tripled on its first trading day.
Figma had previously agreed to be acquired by Adobe for $20 billion in September 2022, but the deal was scrapped in December 2023 over regulatory concerns.
Field launched Figma in 2012 with Brown University classmate Evan Wallace, after being awarded a Thiel Fellowship to drop out and work on the startup full-time.
Figma's largest investors include Index Ventures, Greylock Partners, Kleiner Perkins, and Sequoia Capital.

name: Lionel Messi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Lionel Messi, one of soccer's all-time greats, has starred for decades primarily for FC Barcelona and the Argentine national team.
Raised in Rosario, Argentina, Messi moved to Barcelona at age 13 to join the club's youth program and debuted for its senior team four years later in 2004.
After 17 years in Barcelona, Messi spent two years playing for Paris Saint-German and then moved to the U.S. to join Inter Miami in 2023.
Inter Miami offered him the option to acquire an equity stake in the team when he retires as part of a package deal to lure him to Major League Soccer.
Messi led Argentina to an elusive World Cup title in 2022 after coming up short in his first four tries in soccer's most prestigious tournament.
He has earned an estimated $1.8 billion on and off the field throughout his career, before taxes and agents' fees, and has a lifetime endorsement deal with Adidas.

name: Yuan Zhimin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Yuan Zhimin is founder of Shanghai-listed Kingfa Sci & Tech, a supplier of modified plastics.
In 2020, due to the global pandemic, the company expanded into the production of medical and protective gloves.
Yuan, who holds a graduate degree from the Beijing Institute of Technology, founded the company in 1993.
Yuan's son, Yuan Changchang, was appointed vice chairman of Kingfa in 2024.

name: Trae Stephens
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: An early employee at Palantir, cofounder and board chairman Peter Thiel called Stephens one day to recruit him to Thiel's VC firm Founders Fund.
Trae Stephens is ranked at No. 7 on the 2026 Midas List, his 3rd appearance.

Stephens cofounded the defense tech company Anduril in 2017 alongside Oculus founder Palmer Luckey.  Stephens remains executive chairman of the company which was last valued at $61 billion in May 2026.
Stephens led Founders Fund's investment in the supply chain logistics platform Flexport, valued at $3.8 billion after dipping from its $8 billion peak in 2022
Stephens is also a cofounder of Sol, a startup making eyeglasses with Kindle-style lenses for "immersive reading."
He began his career in the office of then-Congressman Rob Portman and in the Political Affairs Office at the Afghan embassy in Washington, D.C.

name: Anatoly Lomakin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2010-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Anatoly Lomakin started out trading chemicals and sharing an office with future billionaire Vladimir Potanin.
In 1992 he persuaded three of the largest post-Soviet producers of fertilizer--Silvinit, Uralkali and Belaruskali--to unite.
In 2010 Lomakin and his partners sold their stakes in Silvinit, Russia's second-largest producer of potassium fertilizer, for roughly $3 billion.
Today Lomakin owns 50% of Investstroy, a company that invests in housing and residential property development.
forbes_facts: Anatoly Lomakin became a Yedinaya Rossiya party deputy in Russia's State Duma in 2012 but stepped down less than a year later, citing health problems.
The only law that he voted for during his time in the Duma was one prohibiting the adoption of Russian children by U.S. citizens.

name: Thongma Vijitpongpun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2013-2024); Hurun Global (2014-2022)
forbes_bio: Civil engineer Thongma Vijitpongpun founded Pruksa in 1993 and built it intoThailand's biggest property developer of low-to-middle income housing.
Pruksa, which is known for its affordable prefab townhouses, went public in 2005.
In a 2016 restructuring, Thongma delisted Pruksa Real Estate and formed a new holding outfit, Pruksa Holding.
In February 2023, he stepped down as group CEO but remains vice chairman of the company.
forbes_facts: As a youngster, he helped his father hawk fish-maw soup.
Thongma enjoys reading books on Buddhist philosophy.

name: Bui Thanh Nhon
forbes_bio: Bui Thanh Nhon is chairman of the Nova Group, whose flagship is real estate company No Va Land Investment Group.
The group's other interests include consumer goods, entertainment and food and beverage.
He used to work for the government before venturing out on his own in 1992, with a company selling animal feed and medicine.
He got into real estate in 2007 with a condo project in Ho Chi Minh City.
